Engine notes: 32:14 Amal 'زعلتكش عن' = she said عن; 38:47 Amal 'ريم' = غيم; 43:06 Amal 'بهدئ' = بيحرق; 05:51/06:00 'شوب' = shoab (heat), not English shop; 19:41 'قير لاو' = غير لو. laazem_noun 12:56 is not a slip: he went on to أنا لازم أدير بالي على محلي himself (13:20). Left out: 05:34 'تلات إلا تلت' vs her chat 'tentain illa tult' - her only voiced reply was 'Nice', so no signal (could be engine or a time-word slip); 06:27 'بنقلق؟' was a question and Amal said either form works (adjective or I worry); 30:11 'mara-mara-maratat' is a stutter on مطرت (S5); 30:29 ثلاث مرة -> ثلاث مرات was his own self-fix; 06:51 قلقان -> قلقانين self-fix; 50:27 حجور/حجرات -> حجار self-fix; 18:47 سجر for فجر is also a root-letter slip (S4) - filed only as the didn't-know of فجر. 06:10 'شوي dangerous' not tier 3 (dangerous not on her sheet). Latin stretches: 03:07 amalit tilha (ok, chat 3meltelha), 04:49 alayhi salmik (= allah ysallmik, she said Yes), 46:03 nadafet, 55:29-1:00:00 meta talk about mufaddal mostly English.

rows.why: Talking about his fiancee he used the masculine adjective; Amal echoed back the feminine عيانة؟ (the line got cut by his connection).
Same masculine adjective for a feminine noun again after her 02:00 fix; she recast to عيانة and he repeated 'Yeah, عيانة' - its own slip per GR-32.
rows.english: My fiancee is a bit sick

rows.why: He put the verb before the subject راسها (added after); Amal recast the order, he repeated at 04:07 (repeat, not counted).

rows.medi_said: I don't know how to say cough. She has a cough.
rows.amal_said: They say but كح. I say كحة.
rows.why: He said he did not know the word for cough; Amal supplied كحة.

rows.medi_said: الـ or لا الـ نار. ... لـ النار for fire
rows.amal_said: You're worried from. ... You're worried about. You're worried from. ... Men، men.
rows.why: قلقان takes من; he tried لـ and Amal told him (in English) it is 'worried from', then من; he took it ('We would say من, right?').

rows.amal_said: no. There's another word for that.
rows.right: (another verb for a fire starting - not given)
rows.why: For 'a fire will start' he tried يبدأ; Amal said no, there is another word, and set it aside.
دير بال takes على; he joined خطيبتي straight on and Amal recast with على (phrase was new this lesson, so medium).
rows.english: I took care of my fiancee

rows.why: Dropped على again after her 09:51 fix; Amal named the rule 'بدير بالي takes على' and he said it right at 11:50.
rows.english: I took care of my fiancee

rows.amal_said: دير بالك is actually the command form.
rows.why: The 'your' ending on بال is -ak (بالك), not -eek; Amal gave دير بالك and told him it is the command form.
After خلينا the next verb is the bare present; he used the past عملنا and Amal said نعمل, which he repeated.

rows.medi_said: الدرس إنه، uh, إنه تخطط-- uh, تخططي.
rows.why: He meant 'the lesson that you planned' (he says so at 15:13) but used إنه for illi; Amal only asked what he meant and moved on.
He meant 'you planned' (past) but used the present تخططي; he noticed ('I need to do planned') but never fixed it and Amal did not supply it.

rows.medi_said: Oh, is it, is it، is it عصافير؟ ... أنا نسيته.
rows.why: He guessed عصافير for sky as a question, Amal said that is birds, he said he forgot and she supplied سما (didn't-know; sky = Sama on her sheet).
Listing what is in the sky he gave a singular; Amal asked 'just one?' and he gave the plural غيوم.

rows.medi_said: When, when do you look at the sky? When do you watch the sky?
rows.amal_said: No، امتى بتتطلع على الشمس would be when do you watch the sky؟ امتى الشمس بتطلع؟
rows.right: بتطلع = come up (when does the sun rise)
rows.why: He understood her امتى الشمس بتطلع as 'when do you look at the sky'; Amal said no, that would be بتتطلع على, hers is when does the sun come up.
rows.english: When does the sun come up?

rows.medi_said: Uh, أنا نسيت الكلمة ... بس سجر. سجر؟
rows.amal_said: فجر. You could have just said الصبح بكير بس مش مشكلة.
rows.why: He said he forgot the word (guessed Azan, then سجر?); Amal supplied فجر - a didn't-know.
Engine wrote قير لاو = غير لو; he added لو (if) to 'other than' and Amal said 'No لو. غير.'

rows.amal_said: بس غير شمس و يوم. ... غير شمس و يوم.
rows.why: After 8eir the noun goes bare; Amal recast twice as غير شمس and he then asked about the el- rule and said غير شمس at 20:52.
rows.english: other than the sun and clouds

rows.chat: el-sma billail fi el-2amar u njoom, u 3itme
rows.why: The known sky needs el- and comes first; Amal recast to السما بالليل and he repeated it.
One goes after the noun (or alone); he put واحدة first and Amal only kept واحدة without comment.
After a feminine noun taani must be تانية; Amal echoed his تاني, he changed it to تانية and she approved (مهم).
The fronted نجمة needs a pointer on the verb; Amal said 'point it back' and he fixed to بشوفها ('I forgot the pointer rule').
rows.english: This is the first star I see today

rows.medi_said: since is لسـ-- لسا, right? ... Is it لا؟ ... What's since?
rows.amal_said: No. ... No. Since-- لا is until. ... من.
rows.why: He asked whether since is لسا / لا, Amal said no twice and supplied من - a didn't-know.
He gave the I-form for 'it rains'; Amal answered with the she-form بتمطر - but it was asked as a question, so low.
He said الأول (the first) for الهوا (the air); Amal recast الهوا هون and, when he asked 'What I say?', told him he said الأول.

rows.medi_said: آآ، غير من because it's comparative, right?
rows.why: 'Different from' is غير عن; engine wrote her reply as زعلتكش عن, she said عن again at 32:21 and he took it ('غير always takes عن').

rows.amal_said: آخر المرة means the last of the time. The end of the time. ... صح. آخر مرة. The last time.
rows.chat: aa5er marra tallajat kaanat 2abel talat sneen
rows.why: aa5er + el- means 'the end of'; for 'the last time' it is آخر مرة, which Amal explained.

rows.chat: aa5er marra tallajat kaanat 2abel talat sneen
rows.why: The subject مرة is feminine so kaan must be كانت; Amal prompted 'مرة is...' and he said 'feminine. كانت.'

rows.amal_said: No. ثلاث سنين الماضيين أو الماضيات would be for the last three years. ... Ago is قبل. So قبل ثلاث سنين.
rows.chat: aa5er marra tallajat kaanat 2abel talat sneen
rows.why: He used الماضي (past) for 'ago'; Amal said no, that means 'the last three years', and 'ago' is قبل.
Right after her قبل ثلاث سنين he said سنان (teeth); she asked what سنان is, he said teeth, she gave سنين - a wrong word repeated after her fix, its own slip.
Wrong shape of the she-past (long -aat ending, no doubled l); Amal recast تَلَّجَت with vowels and he repeated ثلّجت.

rows.amal_said: إيش يعني عجل؟ ... عجا كتير الصباح؟ إيش يعني؟
rows.why: He gave the plural 'they came' for singular الهوا; Amal questioned it twice and he fixed it ('it's singular. Aja ktir').
rows.english: the wind came a lot in the morning

rows.amal_said: إيش يعني؟ ... Tell me it was very strong. The wind was very strong in the mornings.
rows.why: 'The wind came a lot' did not say what he meant; Amal asked 'إيش يعني؟' and steered him in English to 'it was very strong', which he then said (كان قوي كتير).
rows.english: the wind was very strong in the morning

rows.medi_said: El nar, nar heret me. Does that count correct?
rows.why: Repeating her 44:14 sentence he used English 'me' instead of the -ni ending; she recast النار حرقتني (wrong form after her model = own slip).
'I cleaned it' needs the object ending; Amal prompted 'It.' and he said nadafetha, which she repeated نظفتها.
Listing things on the land he gave one rose; Amal's reply (engine وحدات؟, likely 'one?' or 'وردات?') led him to the plural وردات? - unclear audio, low.

rows.medi_said: Is it the bee? Is it the bee plants?
rows.amal_said: Z-z-zبيب is raisins, I think. Is... [laughs] زريعة.
rows.why: He could not find the word for plants; Amal supplied زريعة (sheet: plants (domestic) | Zri3a).
For dirt under the ground he tried رمل; Amal said that is sand, then he found تراب and she confirmed 'تراب is dirt or soil'.

rows.medi_said: I always forget this word. ... Does it start with a T? ... أنا بعرف، ما بعرف.
rows.why: He could not recall stones; Amal supplied حجر (sheet: stone | 7ajar).
He meant the old streets in America (plural) and used singular الشارع with a feminine adjective; Amal recast الشوارع and he repeated it.
The adjective after الشوارع needs el- to stay a phrase; Amal confirmed the word and added el-, he repeated الإدام (he said it as a question, so low).

rows.amal_said: Or just حجر. Are stone. ... Made of is different than made.
rows.proposed_rule: To say what something is made of, put the material straight after it as the predicate - no عمل + مع: الشوارع القدام في أمريكا حجر.
rows.why: He built 'were made with stone' as عملت مع حجر; Amal dropped it to just حجر and explained 'made of is different than made' - no bucket covers passive/material.
rows.english: The old streets in America are (made of) stone

rows.amal_said: تاني حجر or الحجر التاني. You said it first right.
rows.why: noun + taani without el- means 'another stone', not 'the second stone'; Amal gave تاني حجر or الحجر التاني.

rows.amal_said: So you could either say my favorite stone or my favorite using عندي. المفضل عندي. ... Never takes pronoun ending.
rows.proposed_rule: mufaddal (favorite) is an adjective and never takes a possessive ending: say المفضل عندي or put the ending on the noun (حجري المفضل).
rows.why: He put the 'my' ending on مفضل; Amal gave المفضل عندي and at 54:56 named the rule 'never takes pronoun ending'.

rows.medi_said: مفضل-- مفضل عندي أو مفضل لي يعني؟
rows.why: Amal's reply opened with a bare 'الـ' prompt (GR-25 A1) then المفضل عندي; but his line was an 'X or Y?' question, so low.

rows.medi_said: I was gonna say الـ مفضل حجر.
rows.amal_said: الحجر المفضل or حجري المفضل. المفضل is an adjective.
rows.why: He put the adjective before the noun; Amal said المفضل is an adjective and goes after: الحجر المفضل.

rows.medi_said: Yeah، okay. So الـ حجري الـ مفضل.
rows.why: A noun with a possessive ending never takes el-; Amal said 'No ال first' and he said حجري المفضل.

rows.amal_said: But al-mufaddal is an adjective, so it follows ders. ... هاد الدرس المفضل عندي.
rows.why: For 'this lesson is my favorite' the adjective needs el- to match الدرس; Amal named it ('it follows ders') and gave المفضل.

rows.why: For 'isn't here' he used في (there is) instead of هون; Amal said 'مش في. مش هون' and explained في is 'there is'.
